enso.cpc_discussion: ENSO Alert System Status: El Niño Advisory   Synopsis:   El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance). El Niño strengthened further last month, with sea surface temperature anomalies exceeding +4.0°C in portions of the eastern equatorial Pacific [Fig. 1] . Most Niño indices increased in the past month, reaching +2.1°C in Niño-3.4, +3.0°C in Niño-3, and +3.9°C in Niño-1+2 [Fig. 2] . The equatorial subsurface temperature index (average from 180°-100°W) was well above average [Fig. 3] , reflecting a deeper-than-average thermocline. Subsurface temperatures remained in excess of +10.0°C at depth in the eastern Pacific Ocean [Fig. 4] . Low-level westerly wind anomalies and upper-level easterly wind anomalies stretched from the western to the east-central equatorial Pacific. Enhanced convection and rainfall persisted from the central to the eastern Pacific, while anomalies remained suppressed over Indonesia [Fig. 5] . The traditional and equatorial Southern Oscillation indices were significantly negative. Collectively, the coupled ocean-atmosphere system reflected a strengthening El Niño. The CPC Official ENSO outlook , which synthesizes multiple models from North America and abroad, indicates El Niño will continue to strengthen through the end of the year [Figs. 6 -7 -8] . notes: Wind/gust ranges: quantile-boosted models widened by a conformal margin fit on out-of-fold errors (days 1-10 ensemble model).

Temperature ranges: NBM high/low plus the empirical error distribution (by lead day and season) measured at Alamogordo, Holloman and Las Cruces airports; the same error spread is assumed at Hawk St, the Pass and Cloudcroft (mountain sites are not verified).
Rain: percentile amounts come from the hurdle model; coverage above nominal mostly reflects the large share of dry days. Cloudcroft days 8-10 slightly under-cover (88% vs 90%).
Test period: Jul 2025 – Oct 2026 (about 15 months), so coverage numbers carry a few points of sampling noise.

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service El Paso TX/Santa Teresa NM
524 PM MDT Mon Oct 26 2026

...New AVIATION...

.KEY MESSAGES... 
Updated at 524 PM MDT Mon Oct 26 2026

 - Slight chance of showers and thunderstorms continue for
   Hudspeth and Otero Counties this evening.

 - A brief stretch of drier weather Tuesday and Wednesday before
   rain chances return Thursday into next weekend. Localized
   flooding is possible later in the week.

 - Temperatures will remain near normal with lowland highs in the 
   lower to mid 70s.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 1114 AM MDT Mon Oct 26 2026

WV imagery shows one short wave over eastern New Mexico and 
continuing to lift northeast, while another short wave just south of 
the CWA will move into the eastern CWA this afternoon. This feature 
could allow a few thunderstorms to develop, mostly over Otero and 
Hudspeth Counties this afternoon and evening. Moisture and 
instability still look respectable, so a few of these storms could 
approach severe (mainly for hail). 

Looks like we should finally get a brief break from the rain and 
storms for Tuesday and Wednesday as west flow and drier air set up 
across the area south of the upper low cutting through the Pac NW 
and northern Rockies. Temperatures should remain just above normal. 

Thursday into the weekend...sub-tropical jet becomes more active and 
brings several impulses across the eastern Pacific to northern 
Mexico and our CWA. This will turn upper flow more southwest while 
mid-level flow turns more southerly and begins bringing more sub-
tropical moisture back to the area. One impulse moves up to the CWA 
Thursday afternoon/evening to return a chance of 
showers/thunderstorms to the area. Another short wave moves in 
Friday for another chance of rain late in the day. Saturday may be 
dry as it looks like the day in-between systems. A better defined 
trough moves toward the area Sunday reaching SoCal by Sunday 
afternoon with a chance of rain in the west late in the day. This 
period with the showers/thunderstorms looks to have less potential 
for severe weather than we have experienced the past several days. 
GFS shows only very modest CAPE values and shear environment looks 
relatively weak. 

The trough moves through the area Monday for area wide chances of 
rain, with models then showing a longer period of dry weather after 
Monday. 

&&

.AVIATION...
(00Z TAFS)
Issued at 520 PM MDT Mon Oct 26 2026

VFR conditions prevail through the period. Slight chance (10-20%) of
a stray shower or storm near KELP overnight. Otherwise, dry
through tomorrow and mainly SKC. Winds AOB 6kts through AM, then
gusting to upper teens at KTCS late in period.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 1114 AM MDT Mon Oct 26 2026

Not much in the way of concerns for fire weather this week, as other 
than a brief dry spell Tuesday and Wednesday, we remain in the 
pattern for chances of rain through the weekend. There will a slight 
chance of thunderstorms this evening over the Sacramento/Capitan 
Mtns this evening before the mid-week dry spell. No significant 
winds are expected this week outside of erratic winds near 
thunderstorms. 

Min RHs: Lowlands 25% west to 45% east through Wednesday, increasing 
to 40s-50% all lowlands Thursday into the weekend.
Gila/Black Range...25-35% through Thursday increasing to 50-70% 
Friday and the weekend. Sacramento/Capitan Mtns...40-55% through 
Thursday, increasing to 55-75% Friday and the weekend. Vent rates 
poor-fair through Saturday.
